accuracy.evidence: Matches the kind, specific, helpful critique protocol (Berger, Austin's Butterfly) and Hattie and Timperley's finding that feedback works when it is about the task and the next step, not the self. Praise of the person ('you're a brilliant writer') is correctly treated as low-value self-level feedback, and the right to set aside advice that does not fit the task follows feedback-literacy research (Carless and Boud).

misconceptions.evidence: Tackles the belief that blunt equals honest and helpful (rubbish and too-short-and-boring options), that kind but vague praise is useful (It's good, Cool poster), that every suggestion must be obeyed (comic strip for a letter, challenge question), and that one critical comment means the whole piece is bad (delete the whole thing). The adult text names defending, excusing and blaming as the typical receiving slips.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaggivefb has four social-skill mechanics not used in any other flagship: a three-way sort of real comments, assembling feedback by dragging a star and then a step onto a piece of work, choosing replies that move two live meters (work gets better, they'll help again), and judging tips against a stated task into use, ask or set aside. Highest 6-token overlap with any lab is 9%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Children learn by choosing and seeing the consequence: a vague star returns 'kind, but which part?', a blunt step is rejected because it is about the person, and a defensive reply drains both meters while 'Which part lost you?' fills them. In the decide step, the comic tip only lands in set aside once the learner checks it against the letter task, so the rule comes from the action.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions before tasks: whether 'It's good' is helpful (the kind option is tempting; the sort shows it is vague), whether the best first move after criticism is to explain it is not your fault (the meters drain when you defend), and whether you must change everything someone suggests (the set-aside bin disproves it). Each done message refers back to the choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six shuffled challenge questions, every wrong option with its own reason: 'It is not unkind at all. The problem is it is vague', 'Hitting back starts a fight. Ask which part, so you can fix it', 'You can say no without being unkind. Say thanks, then set it aside'. Lab wrong taps give the same targeted reasons, not a generic try-again.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation is Flesch-Kincaid grade 2.4 and adult 7.2, under the learner limits of 6.5 and 9.5. Star and step are defined once and reused across the lab, practice and mastery; comments are short, realistic sentences a 9 to 11 year old would hear in class peer review.

no_filler.evidence: Each paragraph carries a rule (specific, about the work), a script (Thanks. Which part lost you?) or a decision rule (does it fit my task). No overlap with Responding to Writing Feedback, which is about adding missing words and details at ages 5 to 7; this lesson is about the feedback exchange itself, and explanation overlap with every lesson is under 1%.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in dark and light: the three bins fit side by side with sorted cards listed inside, the star and step options are full-width cards at least 44 px tall, the two meters sit under the comment, and the decide bins show the task line above them. The longest comment wraps to three lines without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task finishes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge appears, and axe-core reports no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme, with no console errors. Every drag has a labelled button twin, and meter changes and results are announced through the live region and canvas aria-label.
